/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 21 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2964 (-41)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4834 (-46)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2276 (-98)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1571 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 846 (-2)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the day on a slightly softer overall footing, although underlying sentiment remained mixed as strong Pacific activity continued to contrast with quieter conditions in the Atlantic. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $425 to settle at $43,838. C5 remained broadly stable with only a marginal dip of $0.030 to $15.265, while C3 also held relatively flat, easing slightly by $0.173 to $36.150. In the Pacific, activity remained busy throughout the session, continuing the strong fixing volumes seen so far this week. Three miners were active on C5 today, helping to maintain healthy underlying momentum despite tonnage not tightening as aggressively as many had anticipated. Fixtures were reported progressively higher through the day, with one miner fixing around $15.05 for 6/8 June laycans, another paying $15.25 for 8/10 June dates, and reports later in the session suggesting a third miner had paid in the $15.45-$15.50 range for 4/5 June stem. Overall, the market continued along the firmer trajectory that has characterised much of the week. In contrast, Atlantic sentiment remained more subdued. Ballasting routes felt quieter overall, although underlying support persisted due to the still notably tight C3 ballaster supply. Offers for mid-June C3 cargoes were heard in the $36s, though bidding interest remained limited through much of the day, contributing to the softer tone across the basin.
PANAMAX
The sector experienced another negative day, with sentiment remaining generally weak across both Atlantic and Asian markets. The sentiment in Atlantic continued to soften today, with cargo volumes remaining thin and the lengthy tonnage list still weighing on rates. In the Pacific, further losses were observed as we moved towards the end of the trading week, and it feels as though a stronger finish or a decent replenishment of cargoes is needed to steady the market. The Alpha Discovery (82,057 2016) fixed retro Kandla on 13 May via EC South America to Singapore-Japan with grains at around $23,500 to $24,000 by Bunge, although further details were not disclosed. All these reflected on index and the BPI time charter average fell by $882 to $20,485.
SUPRAMAX
Two sides of the coin for the sector today. The Atlantic although was still described as positional but some felt that there was renewed demand from the US Gulf for fronthaul. That said, some still felt that more enquiry was required. Brokers maintained that demand was still in play from the Continent-Mediterranean, again however fresh fixture information was lacking. By contrast the Asian arena was again a subdued affair and rates remained under downward pressure with a good amount of prompt tonnage further south. Further north, the SSI Resolute (63,856 2022) open CJK 27 May was heard fixed to West Africa with steels and deck cargo at close to $25,000 but it later surfaced from others it was closer to $22,500. The Clarke Quay (63,340 2020) open Japan spot was heard to have been placed on subjects at $20,000 for a NoPac round but no more details surfaced. The Norse Growth (66,325 2025) open Koh Sichang 23/24 May was also heard fixed in the $19,000s for an Australia grain round. The Jabal Samhan (63,658 2015) was reported fixed basis delivery Jingtang trip via North China intention steels redelivery Indonesia at $18,750 with Hong Glory. Period activity came to light, there was talk of the Desert Puma (63,654 2025) Saint Nicholas, Greece fixing 8-10 months trading redelivery worldwide at $19,600 with Norden. The 11TC registered a slight gain of $74 at $19,863.

HANDYSIZE
Following on from yesterday, it was another subdued day with little activity emerging. The BHSI slipped by 2 points to 846, while the 7TC average fell by $32 to close at $15,224. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained muted and sentiment largely positional, with rates mostly tracking previous fixtures. The South Atlantic continued to show a soft tone, with the market lacking firm support, while the US Gulf saw fixtures concluded at levels close to the last done. From Asia, there was limited fresh information, with some sources indicating that although the tonnage count is ticking down slightly, there is still insufficient cargo volume to lift the market. As a result, rates are being recorded around last-done levels.

Atlantic
The Agia Dynami (35,220 2010) was placed on subjects for a trip, delivery Barranquilla 26/27 May redelivery Tampa with coal at around $11,000–$11,500 by WBC, although further details were not disclosed. The WL Palekh (37,648 2014) fixed from Progreso 29/30 May for delivery SW Pass to redelivery UK with grains at $18,000 although some sources suggest $19,000 to Falcon. The Great Cosmos (38,649 2018) fixed from EC South America for a fronthaul trip in the low $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed. The Lowlands Engel (40,056 2023) open Santo Tomas end of May fixed delivery US Gulf for an inter-Caribbean trip with grains at close to $19,000, again with no further details available. In addition, Eco Cerberus (37,875 2021) was heard failed for a trip from the East Mediterranean to Florida at $10,500 plus $140,000 ILOHC with cement and the Benjamas Naree (33,780 2012) also failed a trip from Chesapeake to Continent at $19,000 by Norden, although further details were not confirmed.

Asia
Oceanic Praise (37,431 2015) open Kobe on 20/21 May was heard fixed for a trip to the South in the $17,000s. It was also heard that another handysize vessel, open Chittagong fixed via EC India to SE Asia at around $8,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
EU Approves Tougher Import Rules for Steel

The European Parliament has approved stricter steel import curbs as Europe looks to shield domestic producers from growing global oversupply, particularly from China, newswires report. From July 1, tariff-free steel import quotas will be cut by 47% from the 2024 regulation to 18.3 Mt per year, while tariffs on volumes above the quota will rise from 25% to 50%. The regulation would also introduce a “smelting and casting” rule to enhance traceability and limit circumvention through minimal processing in third countries. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场21日继续承压，BDI下跌41点至2964，各船型指数走势分化。Capesize太平洋市场活跃但大西洋偏弱，C5航线维持在$15.265；Panamax和Handysize指数延续跌势，FFA市场Cape和PMX曲线远月走强，显示短期悲观但中长期预期改善。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场太平洋端受矿商支撑保持活跃，C3大西洋 ballast偏紧限制下行空间；Panamax买卖双方僵持，吨位供给充足压制费率；Supramax大西洋端出现美国湾回暖迹象，亚洲持续低迷。FFA曲线整体backwardation结构收窄，反映市场对中期需求担忧缓解。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: C5 Pacific升水结构稳固，矿商积极定载支撑现货；C3大西洋端报价$36但买盘稀疏；Supramax US Gulf fronthaul需求初现；Handysize亚洲吨位微降但货量不足抑制反弹。FFA Cape 6月合约逆势涨$625至41350，显示期货市场看好短期触底。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3大西洋ballaster供给何时释放，突破$36阻力需更多货盘支撑；Supramax US Gulf fronthaul若持续放量或带动小船型回暖；Cape FFA可尝试6/7月价差做收敛；Panamax远期曲线Q4在18000-18450区间具有支撑。
